key_insight: MedVTok introduces a shared visual language for medical AI, mapping both 2D images and 3D volumes from diverse imaging modalities into one unified token space.
problem_solved: Existing medical visual tokenizers are often specific to an imaging modality or data dimension, creating fragmented representations that are difficult to reuse across multimodal systems.
method: Introduce a general-purpose medical visual tokenizer called MedVTok.
Map heterogeneous 2D images and 3D volumes into a unified token space.
Provide a common visual interface for multimodal patient-condition modeling; architectural and training details are not available in the supplied, truncated abstract.
impact: A shared tokenizer could reduce the need for separate modality-specific interfaces and simplify representation reuse in medical AI. The supplied abstract does not include results demonstrating these benefits.
visual_elements: Convergence diagram: diverse medical images and volumes flow into MedVTok, then into shared visual tokens.
Before-and-after comparison: fragmented modality-specific tokenizers versus one common visual interface.
Side-by-side icons of a 2D image and a 3D volume to emphasize dimensional coverage.
Pipeline graphic: medical imaging → unified tokens → multimodal patient-condition modeling.
paper_title: MedVTok: A General-Purpose Medical Visual Tokenizer
paper_authors: Chenglong Ma, Yuanfeng Ji, Junzhi Ning, Jiyao Liu, Yujie Wei
